First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(3y-{y}^{2}) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =3(1)-2y \\  & =3-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{3-2y}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(0,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(0,3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{3-2(3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-3)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =-\frac{1}{3}\cdot (x-0) \\ y & =-\frac{1}{3}x+3.\end{aligned}
$$
